dataset_info.dataset_name: Insulin content in the head of the pancreas from STS-40
dataset_description: The concentration of insulin in the head of the pancreas from rats flown on STS-40 (SLS-1) tended to be lower than that of STS-58. The insulin concentration for flight animals from STS-40 “immediately” following recovery (F, R+0) was 103.9 +/-11.9 ng/mg (n=10), which was significantly greater (P < 0.02) than flight controls (C, R+0) 58.2 +/- 11.0 ng/mg (n=5). The insulin content of flight animals (F, R+0) was not significantly different from vivarium controls (CV, R+0), 84.9 +/- 9.4 ng/mg (n=5) or basal controls (L+0), 83.4 +/- 12.1 ng/mg (n=5). As with rats from the STS-54 flight, there was no difference between flight animals held for mission-length after recovery (F, R+ML), 97.9 +/- 14.2 ng/mg (n=9) and recovery plus mission-length control animals (C, R+ML: 67.4 +/- 16.3 ng/mg; CV, R+ML: 131.3 +/-9.3 ng/,g).

dataset_info.dataset_name: Average Calbindin-D28k in Animal Groups from SLS-1 and SLS-2
dataset_description:
This spreadsheet shows average kidney calbindin-D28k levels in flight and control animals from SLS-1 and SLS-2.

The results of this study with ELISA of calbindin-D28k did not confirm the reduction in calbindn-D28k found in our earlier study (Sergeev, et al., 1996). Calbindin-D28k levels in kidneys of SLS-1 flight animals after just returning to Earth (R+0), 2.24 +/- 0.17 ug/mg protein, were significantly greater than those of basal controls (L+0), 0.89 +/- 0.06 ug/mg, but not ground controls (GC), 1.97 +/-0.03 (Figure 4). Levels of calbindin-D28k measured by ELISA were equivalent in flight animals immediately following flight (R+0) and after nine days at Earth gravity (R+ML), 1.94 +/- 0.12 ug/mg protein (P=0.5). In SLS-2 animals, renal calbindin-D28k in flight animals after just returning to Earth (R+0), 2.22 +/- 0.27 ug/mg protein, was significantly greater than basal controls (L+0), 1.08 +/- 0.13, (P<0.001) and ground controls, 0.62 +/- 0.04 (P<0.001) (Figure 5). Calbindin-D28k in kidneys of flight animals after return to Earth gravity (R+0) was similar to those of flight animals after 14 days at Earth gravity (R+ML), 2.03 +/- 0.11 (P=0.5) and to animals sacrificed in flight (FD13), 2.75 +/- 0.31 (P=0.06). Thus, the results of this study indicate an increase in calbindin-D28k levels in microgravity. Differences in the results of this and our previous study (Sergeev, et al., 1996) suggest that other factors the animals are exposed to during flight regulate in a substantial way calbindin-D28k. Among these factors may be environmental stresses, such as elevated temperatures (from about 24.5 C to 28.5 C in SLS-2) and reduced humidity (slightly more than 30% to over 100% for SLS-2). Temperature extremes were even greater for SLS-1 (27-32 C).

dataset_info.dataset_name: Calbindin-D28K in Rat Kidney: Data Summary
dataset_description:
Analysis by quantitative immunocytochemistry (QUICC) revealed a significantly higher (by one way analysis of variance) level of calbindin-D28K in animals in space for 16 days on STS-90 plus 1-day at Earth gravity (R+1) compared to asynchronous ground control rats [48 hr delay from experimental group, vivarium, R+3 (P=0.008); 96 hr delay from experimental group, simulation , R+5 (P<0.001], flight animals plus 14-days at Earth gravity (R+14) (P<0.001), and asynchronous ground controls: 15 days delay, vivarium (R+15) (P=0.004); 17 days delay, simulation (R+17) (P=0.008).

Only the flight animals at 1 day following return from on orbit exhibited statistically significant differences from the other groups, including flight animals after 14 days at Earth gravity.

dataset_info.dataset_name: Calbindin-D28k in the rat hypothalamus
dataset_description:
This excel spreadsheet contains a list of slides that are stored in the investigator's laboratory, along with related treatment information.

Sections of hypothalami from STS-56 showed little or no reactivity for calbindin-D28k. This was an unexpected result since calbindin-D28k has previously been described as present in neurons of the ventromedial nucleus, supraoptic nucleus and medial mammillary nucleus of the rat. Because there was weak immunoreactivity for positive control peptides (neuropeptide Y and neurophysin), it is believed that the lengthy storage time in fixative contributed to the diminished immunoreactivity for calbindin-D28k and the control neuropeptides in the hypothalamus. The flight controls as a group showed weaker neurophysin II immunoreactivity than flight animals, however, the flight group exhibited considerable variability in the density of reaction product. Due to weak or absent immunoreactivity in the available tissue specimens, no conclusion can be reached regarding the effect of mg on hypothalamic levels of calbindin-D28k.
